title: Canonical composition comparison for unbounded ringed-topos direct images
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be sites small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention], carrying sheaves of commutative rings $A,B,C$, respectively. Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),B)$ and $g:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E),C)$ be morphisms of ringed topoi: their underlying functors are adjunctions $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ and $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$, the inverse images preserve finite limits, and the structural ring maps are $f^{-1}B\to A$ and $g^{-1}C\to B$. On module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], direct image has underlying abelian direct image with the target-ring action induced by these structural maps. Write $D(A),D(B),D(C)$ for the ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $Rf_*,Rg_*,R(gf)_*$ for the total right derived direct images computed with K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Let $Q$ denote localization of cochain complexes of $A$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\kappa_{g,f}:R(g\circ f)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*Rf_*.$$
Its normalization is as follows: for a K-injective complex $I$ of $A$-modules and a K-injective resolution $j:f_*I\to J$ of $B$-module complexes, the map $g_*f_*I\xrightarrow{g_*j}g_*J$ is a quasi-isomorphism and its class is $\kappa_{g,f,QI}$ under the canonical resolution identifications. These identifications and the comparison are natural in the derived argument.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, label lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, lines 4010-4030; canonical derived-functor comparison on K-injective representatives (the proof uses derived pullback composition and uniqueness of right adjoints)

proof.text: For each of $h=f,g,gf$, the tensor-formula module pullback $h^*$ is left adjoint to the module direct image $h_*$, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Both are additive (their maps preserve sums). Termwise application preserves shifts and the finite biproduct cone differential, so the induced functors on homotopy categories are exact. The cone-triangle description and localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] then make $Qh_*$ exact into the target derived category. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] gives the adjunction on unbounded homotopy categories. The everywhere-defined $Lh^*$ and its K-flat comparison are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. K-injective resolutions exist by the hypothesis and [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to $Qh_*$ on the homotopy category. Thus the right derived comparison $Qh_*I\to Rh_*QI$ is invertible for every K-injective $I$. The existence hypotheses of [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] are now satisfied, giving $Lh^*\dashv Rh_*$. Choose the canonical adjunction of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], whose formula on a fraction $t:P\to M$, a resolution $s:K\to I$, and $a:P\to h_*I$ is the localized underived adjunct, preceded by the left-derived comparison and followed by $Q(s)^{-1}$. This fixes the adjunction, rather than selecting an arbitrary adjunction between the same functors.

source.place: Tag 07A6, label lemma-adjoint; section-unbounded; derived.tex Tags 09T5 and 0FND

proof.text: Identify $(gf)_*$ with $g_*f_*$ on modules. The underlying abelian direct images agree, and the $C$-action on either side is induced by the same composite $f^{-1}g^{-1}C\to f^{-1}B\to A$, so the identification is linear and natural. Compose the two module adjunctions by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Take the inverse image of this identity under the conjugation bijection of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] to obtain the canonical isomorphism $\theta:f^*g^*\xrightarrow{\sim}(gf)^*$. Write $c_h:h^*h_*\to1$ for the underived module counits. By the definition of conjugation and the composite counit formula, $\theta$ satisfies, for every $A$-module complex $I$, the identity $c_{gf,I}\circ\theta_{g_*f_*I}=c_{f,I}\circ f^*(c_{g,f_*I})$. These equations hold termwise on complexes and in the homotopy category, since the adjunctions there are induced termwise.

source.place: Tag 03D8, label lemma-push-pull-composition-modules; the composite counit equation written out

proof.text: Let $M\in D(C)$ and choose $p:P\to M_0$ with $QM_0\cong M$, $P$ K-flat with flat terms, by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], $g^*P$ is again K-flat with flat terms. The comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] therefore identify $Lf^*Lg^*QP$ with $Qf^*g^*P$ and $L(gf)^*QP$ with $Q(gf)^*P$. Compose these identifications with $Q\theta_P$ to obtain $\alpha_{QP}:Lf^*Lg^*QP\xrightarrow{\sim}L(gf)^*QP$. This is natural for all homotopy maps between K-flat complexes: each left-derived comparison is natural and so is $\theta$. Each functor in this comparison inverts quasi-isomorphisms, so clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descends the comparison through the localization of the K-flat subcategory. That localization is equivalent to $D(C)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Consequently it gives a canonical natural isomorphism $\alpha:Lf^*Lg^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(gf)^*$ on all of $D(C)$, independent of $p$. No assertion that arbitrary termwise pullback preserves quasi-isomorphisms is used.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, label lemma-derived-pullback-composition; K-flat localization and naturality made explicit

proof.text: The composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] makes $Lf^*Lg^*$ left adjoint to $Rg_*Rf_*$. Conjugate $\alpha:Lf^*Lg^*\to L(gf)^*$ between this adjunction and $L(gf)^*\dashv R(gf)_*$, using [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Its conjugate is a canonical natural isomorphism $\kappa:R(gf)_*\to Rg_*Rf_*$. Explicitly, if $e_h$ denotes the canonical derived adjunction bijection in the direction from maps into $Rh_*$ to maps out of $Lh^*$, then $\kappa$ is characterized by $e_f(e_g(\kappa_K\circ b))=e_{gf}(b)\circ\alpha_M$ for every $b:M\to R(gf)_*K$. This is precisely the composite hom bijection and the conjugation formula; its inverse is the conjugate of $\alpha^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, label lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; uniqueness of right adjoints as an explicit conjugation

proof.text: Fix a K-injective $A$-module complex $I$, and a quasi-isomorphism $j:f_*I\to J$ with $J$ K-injective over $B$. Use the K-injective comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to identify $R(gf)_*QI$ with $Qg_*f_*I$, $Rf_*QI$ with $Qf_*I$, and $Rg_*Rf_*QI$ with $Qg_*J$. To compare $\kappa_{QI}$ with $Q(g_*j)$ it suffices to compare postcomposition on all maps into $Qg_*f_*I$. Indeed, equality for the identity map already gives equality of their components. For $M=QM_0$, write any such map as $b=Q(a)Q(t)^{-1}$, with $t:P\to M_0$ a quasi-isomorphism and $a:P\to g_*f_*I$, by [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system, lem-pc-right-fraction-representation]. Replace $P$ by a K-flat resolution with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; composing both arrows with that resolution leaves the same fraction. Thus we may assume $P$ K-flat with flat terms, and $g^*P$ has those properties by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat].

source.place: Tag 05RT, label lemma-acyclic (quasi-isomorphisms form a multiplicative system); categories.tex Tag 04VI, label lemma-morphisms-right-localization; K-flat refinement uses sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YS

proof.text: Apply the fraction formula of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] to the $g$-adjunction, with $s=j$, denominator $t$, and map $g_*j\circ a:P\to g_*J$. Under the K-flat comparison $Lg^*M\cong Qg^*P$, it sends $Q(g_*j)\circ b$ to $Q(j)^{-1}\circ Q(c_{g,J}\circ g^*(g_*j\circ a))$. Naturality of the module counit gives $c_{g,J}\circ g^*g_*j=j\circ c_{g,f_*I}$, so this equals $Q(c_{g,f_*I}\circ g^*a)$. Next apply the same fraction formula to the $f$-adjunction, taking resolution $\mathrm{id}_I$ and the K-flat representative $g^*P$ of $Lg^*M$. The resulting map out of $Lf^*Lg^*M\cong Qf^*g^*P$ is $Q(c_{f,I}\circ f^*c_{g,f_*I}\circ f^*g^*a)$. On the other hand, the formula for $e_{gf}(b)$, with resolution $\mathrm{id}_I$ and denominator $t$, gives $Q(c_{gf,I}\circ(gf)^*a)$ out of $L(gf)^*M\cong Q(gf)^*P$. Precomposing with $\alpha_M$ inserts $Q\theta_P$. Naturality of $\theta$ and the counit equation from step 2 give $c_{gf,I}\circ(gf)^*a\circ\theta_P=c_{gf,I}\circ\theta_{g_*f_*I}\circ f^*g^*a=c_{f,I}\circ f^*c_{g,f_*I}\circ f^*g^*a$. Thus $Q(g_*j)$ satisfies exactly the characterization of $\kappa_{QI}$ in step 4 for every $b$, and equals $\kappa_{QI}$. The inverse $Q(j)^{-1}$ was used only in $D(B)$; $f_*I$ was never assumed K-injective.

source.place: Tag 0FND, label lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general, fraction adjunction calculation; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6E normalization expanded by the worker

proof.text: Since $\kappa_{QI}$ is an isomorphism and equals $Q(g_*j)$, [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] implies $H^n(Q(g_*j))$ is an isomorphism for every integer $n$. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], these maps identify with $H^n(g_*j)$, so $g_*j$ is a quasi-isomorphism, as asserted. For a different K-injective resolution $j':f_*I\to J'$, the bijection [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] lifts the derived comparison $Qj'\circ(Qj)^{-1}:QJ\to QJ'$ to a unique homotopy class $h:J\to J'$, with $hj$ homotopic to $j'$. Applying the additive $g_*$ preserves this homotopy by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy], and hence $Q(g_*h)Q(g_*j)=Q(g_*j')$. These are exactly the resolution identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. Finally $\alpha$ and its conjugate $\kappa$ are natural on the derived categories by steps 3 and 4. Therefore the representative formula just proved respects all derived morphisms and all resolution identifications, giving the required naturality and normalization.
